analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of a test-only file, provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/EngineV2BridgeTests.swift. No production code changed in the supplied evidence. The changed ranges are small: the test tokenizer's decodeTable (lines 146-155), a new stopStringScope parameter on makeBridge (lines 440/459), and new scoped stop-sequence tests (lines 811-896). The supplied excerpts, lines 1267-2447, are unchanged context from the same file.

I examined the surrounding tests against T-041, A-001 and TB-007:
- Queue-full and token-budget error classification, which feeds the 429/503 reroute.
- Shared GlobalKVCacheBudget reservation and release on finish, teardown, engine rejection, overflow and cancellation.
- SSD staging reservations and fallback to a cold reservation.
- Cancellation fan-out through EngineV2Runtime.
- The fail-loud factory with refusal telemetry and no fallback.
- The retired-env detection, which confirms DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_DISK_GB and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL stay live knobs.

These tests assert fail-closed behavior: reservations are released, no plaintext is exposed, and no capacity is over-admitted. They do not weaken any control or alter the cache TTL, HMAC naming or scope handling described in T-041. Test fixtures use temp directories, scripted memory snapshots and a scripted engine, so they add no runtime attack surface.

Limits: the production scoped-stop-sequence implementation (ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope and EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence) and the rest of the patch are not in these units. The patch excerpt is truncated, so any security effect of the stop-scope logic, for example on output truncation or leakage of reasoning-channel text, needs review in the production-source units. Nothing in these units identifies a regression.
